[0] A significant beneficial effect (12-13%) was also observed using the C23-GAL4 transverse muscle driver.

[1] Global overexpression of GCLc was shown to increase life span significantly (15%).

[2] Knockdown of GCLc by 30-70% using an RNAi-hairpin strategy had a significant effect, resulting in greater sensitivity to H2O2 and reduced survivorship under normal conditions varying from a 50% reduction in median life span to lethality.

[3] Neuronal overexpression of GCLc (Appl-GAL4 and D42-GAL4 neuronal drivers) in a long-lived background extended mean and maximum life spans up to 50%, without affecting the rate of oxygen consumption by the flies. Positive effects were also observed with the elav-GAL4 driver, but these effects were consistently significant (p < 0.05) only for the elav/GCLc5 genotype.

[4] Neuronal overexpression of GCLc (Appl-GAL4 and D42-GAL4 neuronal drivers) in a long-lived background extended mean and maximum life spans up to 50%, without affecting the rate of oxygen consumption by the flies. Positive effects were also observed with the elav-GAL4 driver, but these effects were consistently significant (p < 0.05) only for the elav/GCLc5 genotype.

[5] Neuronal overexpression of GCLc (Appl-GAL4 and D42-GAL4 neuronal drivers) in a long-lived background extended mean and maximum life spans up to 50%, without affecting the rate of oxygen consumption by the flies. Positive effects were also observed with the elav-GAL4 driver, but these effects were consistently significant (p < 0.05) only for the elav/GCLc5 genotype.

[6] Neuronal overexpression of GCLc (Appl-GAL4 and D42-GAL4 neuronal drivers) in a long-lived background extended mean and maximum life spans up to 50%, without affecting the rate of oxygen consumption by the flies. Positive effects were also observed with the elav-GAL4 driver, but these effects were consistently significant (p < 0.05) only for the elav/GCLc5 genotype.

[7] Expression of GCLc driven by Tub-GAL4 was increased by 4- to 6-fold , in comparison with controls, as revealed by immunoblot analysis (data not shown) and the GCL enzyme activity assay. The experimental groups overexpressing GCLc globally (UAS-GCLc with the Tub-GAL4 driver) exhibited no significant increases in life span, in comparison with their respective controls.

[8] Global overexpression of GCLm (Tub-GAL4 driver) extended the mean life span up to 24%.

[9] Late-onset administration of GDF11 extends life span and delays development of age-related markers in the annual fish Nothobranchius guentheri. Dietary intake of recombinant GDF11 had little influences on the body weight and length of aging fish N. guentheri, but it delayed the development of age-related biomarkers and extended both the median and maximum life span of the fish. It revealed that the maximum lifespans of the experimental and control fish were 56 ± 1.1 and 52 ± 1.4 weeks, respectively (p<0.05), and their mean lifespans were 51 ± 1.4 and 47.1 ± 1.2 weeks, separately (p <0.05). It was found that rGDF11 administration extended the mean and maximum lifespans of the fish by approximately 3.9 and 4 weeks, respectively.

Each numbered passage describes one lifespan experiment. For each, report three things using ONLY that passage:
  organism: the model organism studied, one lowercase word
  direction: exactly one of 'increases lifespan', 'decreases lifespan', or 'no change'
  method: how the gene was altered, e.g. gene knockout, overexpression, mutation, knockdown

Output one block per passage, in order, formatted exactly:
[0]
organism: ...
direction: ...
method: ...

Nothing else. If a passage does not state something, write 'unstated'.
